method: Accepts two through 2,000 signed decimal latitude/longitude waypoints, one pair per line, with latitude in -90 through 90 and longitude in -180 through 180. Each original leg uses its shortest great-circle arc on a sphere of radius 6,371,008.8 m. Haversine central angles determine leg distances; the number of equal steps is ceil(distance / requested spacing), with a relative 1e-12 snap at integer ratios to avoid a floating-point extra step. Intermediate points use spherical linear interpolation of Cartesian unit vectors: A=sin((1-f)delta)/sin(delta), B=sin(f delta)/sin(delta), then atan2 recovers latitude and normalized longitude. Original waypoints and consecutive duplicate points are preserved, shared leg endpoints are emitted once, and antipodal legs are refused because their shortest route is not unique. Spacing must be positive and at most 1,000 km; results above 20,000 points are refused before interpolation. The generated GeoJSON LineString uses longitude/latitude order and six-decimal coordinates. Distances and the longest generated step are computed before that display rounding. This spherical model is for plotting and data preparation, not navigation or surveying. All processing is browser-local.
